newsitem.title: UK: Salomon Bros analysts estimate GAN worth FFr8.5bln.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Bros analysts estimate GAN worth FFr8.5bln.

text.p: Insurance analysts at Salomon Brothers said on Wednesday they believe GAN, the French insurer soon to be sold by the French government, could be worth 8.5 billion francs ($1.3 billion).
"Attempting to value GAN is fraught with difficulty given the company's distressed state and opaque financials," Salomon's said in a market bulletin.

"However we tentatively set out a valuation which indicates a value for the insurance operations of 9.25 billion francs, and a 8.5 billion francs value for the whole of GAN," the bulletin said. Salomon's analyst Brian Shea said his calculations indicate a fair value for GAN's shares on privatisation could be 150 francs, close to their current trading value. But he said he was not tempted to recommend GAN shares as a buy. "Politics is the real driver here. There is nothing that an insurance analyst can really predict for the share price because there is so much volatility," he told Reuters. This is understood to be the first publicised valuation for GAN. Shea highlighted the difficulty in calculating a value for GAN because of its opaque structure, and said his figures should be taken as an example rather than a precise valuation. "It shows that the cost savings in absolute terms don't have to be big in order for there to be a synergy kick," he said. Shea estimated GAN's life operations were worth 4.1 billion francs, using a multiple of 15 on its earnings. Its non-life unit was valued at 3.2 billion francs, using a multiple of 12 on earnings. GAN's 95 percent share in GAN International was assigned a value of 7.6 billion francs, with Shea concluding that 1996 earnings of 321 million francs underestimated the unit's earnings power. A value of 9 billion francs was put on the troubled CIC bank, including its 50 percent ownership of Socapi. "This is the rough price rumoured to have been offered by Societe Generale and BNP late last year. As GAN owns 93 per cent of CIC, this translates to 8.4 billion francs," the bulletin said. Looking at the UIC property financing arm, Salomons assumed that after the state's recapitalisation and guarantees are in place, no further losses will emerge. "As 7.1 billion francs of the state's 11 billion france recapitalisation will go to plug UIC's balance sheet hole, we merely assign a negative 1.7 billion value," the bulletin said. Salomon's also pointed out that there would have to be adjustments for complicated subsidiary cross shareholdings and claims from life insurance policyholders on earnings arising from such stakes. The analysts therefore applied 'haircuts' of 80 per cent to the earnings of CIC, International, and Socapi owned by GAN Vie. "Were it not for GAN's cross shareholdings dilemma, we would value the insurance operations at 16.3 billion francs and the whole company at 17.6 billion francs," Shea said. "As presently structured, we therefore value GAN at 8.5 billion francs, and the insurance operations at 9.25 billion francs," he said. GAN, which is 76-percent state owned, lost 5.7 billion francs last year because of bad real estate involvements. The conservatives in February had to come up with a 20 billion franc bailout plan. That plan must still be approved by the European Commission, and France promised to privatise both GAN and CIC to win that approval. GAN launched the sale of UIC on Wednesday. On Tuesday the European insurance alliance Eureko said it had made a bid to the French government to buy GAN. The French insurer AGF, Allianz AG of Germany, Fortis AG, Assicurazioni Generali SpA of Italy, Zurich Group in Switzerland and ING in the Netherlands, are also candidates for the purchase.
